title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 675-676): Grothendieck builds a group scheme O_N^* (on the next page written \hat\Gamma_N^*) over the base S_0. Its sections are 'units congruent to an invertible class mod N'. It sits in an extension (79): 1 -> (1+12Z)^* -> O_12^* -> (Z/12Z)^*_{S_0} ≅ mu_2 x mu_2 -> 1. The quotient is a constant group scheme. The two projections eps_2 (reduction to (Z/4)^*) and eps_3 (reduction to (Z/6)^* ≅ (Z/3)^*) are recoded through 0/1-valued functions nu_2, nu_3 on the constant scheme {0,1}_{S_0}, with eps_i = (-1)^{nu_i} = 1 - 2 nu_i. Here nu_i are idempotent functions (nu_i^2 = nu_i) and the group law is addition mod 2.

On this page he chooses representatives ±1, ±5 of (Z/12)^* and obtains a set-theoretic section of (79), formula (83): mu_0 = (-5)^{nu_2} 5^{nu_3}. Mod 4 this is (-1)^{nu_2}, and mod 6 it is (-1)^{nu_3}. A general section is then (84): mu = mu_0 + 12 lambda_0, with (nu_2, nu_3) a section of {0,1}x{0,1} and lambda_0 a section of G_a. So each fibre of O_12^* -> (Z/12)^* is an affine line, and the identity component is 1 + 12 G_a.

He then writes mu_0 as a polynomial in the idempotents:
- 5^{nu_3} = 1 + 4 nu_3.
- (-5)^{nu_2} = (1 - 2 nu_2)(1 + 4 nu_2) = 1 + 2 nu_2 - 8 nu_2^2 = 1 - 6 nu_2, using nu_2^2 = nu_2.
- Hence (85): mu_0 = (1 + 4 nu_3)(1 - 6 nu_2) = 1 + 4 nu_3 - 6 nu_2 - 24 nu_2 nu_3.

A struck-out attempt used the simpler representative mu_0' = 1 + 4 nu_3 - 6 nu_2. On the next page this becomes the normal form mu = 1 + 4 nu_3 - 6 nu_2 + 12(nu_0 - 2 nu_2 nu_3), and he rewrites mu in mod-4 and mod-6 adapted forms.

Purpose: explicit coordinates on an integral group-scheme model of the units of Z/N-type congruence data. This is analogous to the decomposition Z_2^* = {±1} x (1+4Z_2), done here simultaneously for 2 and 3, and probably serves the arithmetic of level-N structures in the 'Longue Marche' sequel.
errors: The table (82) is inconsistent with (83) and with (88) on the next page. Since 5 ≡ 1 mod 4 and 5 ≡ -1 mod 3, the class 5 has eps_2 = +1, eps_3 = -1 (nu_2 = 0, nu_3 = 1). The table instead puts +5 at (nu_2 = 1, nu_3 = 0) and -5 at (nu_2 = 0, nu_3 = 1), so the off-diagonal entries are swapped. Formula (83), mu_0 = (-5)^{nu_2} 5^{nu_3}, is the correct one.
Minor (next page): in (86) the bracket should contain -6 nu_2 nu_3, not -3 nu_2 nu_3, if the transcription there is accurate. All computations on this page itself are correct.

ideas.what: Group scheme of units mod N over a base as an extension of the constant group (Z/N)^* by the congruence subgroup 1+N·G_a. Each coset is an affine line.
ideas.modern_name: Dilatation / congruence group scheme (cf. deformations of G_a to G_m with law x+y+λxy)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Néron-type dilatations; Waterhouse–Weisfeiler, Sekiguchi–Oort–Suwa for the λ-deformation

ideas.what: Writing a section of a constant group scheme via idempotent 0/1 functions and expressing (-5)^{nu}, 5^{nu} as polynomials using nu^2 = nu.
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial interpolation on finite constant schemes / idempotent calculus

ideas.what: Set-theoretic splitting of (Z/12)^* ≅ mu_2 x mu_2 by representatives ±1, ±5, with CRT-compatible signs mod 4 and mod 3.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an explicit, elementary coordinate computation (choice of coset representatives and idempotent polynomial identities) inside a larger construction of congruence group schemes. It is correct apart from a swapped table entry, and contains nothing new beyond bookkeeping.
